raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through. I'm planning for my wheat and maize this year on the same 30.4 mu — that's how we do it here, winter wheat first then summer maize right after.

---

**My thinking (as the farmer):**

I've been doing wheat-maize for 30 years, same as my father. The land is decent but not the best in the village. My wife helps in the field, one of my sons works in town at a factory so he sends money but can only come back at busy times — wheat harvest, maize planting. My daughter is still in school. So it's mostly me and my wife doing the day-to-day, and I hire the combine for wheat harvest like everyone else.

**Wheat (winter wheat, 30.4 mu):**
I'll plant around October 10-15, same as always. Last year I got about 450 kg/mu, which was okay — not my best year but not bad. The neighbor Old Zhang got nearly 500 but he puts more fertilizer. I usually put down one bag of compound fertilizer (50 kg) per mu before planting — that's about 15-15-15 — so roughly 7-8 kg each of N, P, K from the base. Then at jointing in early spring when the wheat starts shooting up, I topdress with urea, about half a bag per mu, maybe 25 kg urea which gives another 11 kg N. So total N is around 18-19 kg/mu. Costs too much to put more, and honestly more doesn't always help — two years ago I tried extra urea and just got lodging.

Irrigate: usually 3 times for wheat — once before winter (overwintering water), once at jointing, once at heading. If spring rains are good I might skip heading, but I can't count on rain here. Pumping from the well costs money, electric is metered.

Seed I buy from the co-op, a common variety everyone plants, Jimai or similar. Maybe 10 kg/mu to be safe — I prefer thicker stands.

Pesticide: I spray herbicide once in spring for the broadleaf weeds, and if I see aphids at heading I'll spray an insecticide. Usually both.

**Maize (summer maize, same 30.4 mu):**
Right after wheat harvest around June 10-15, I need to get maize in fast — can't let the field sit, the growing season is short here. I do no-till direct seeding with the hired planter, it's the only way to get it done in a week. Hybrid seed, I buy certified seed each year, can't save hybrid seed.

Fertilizer: one shot of compound at planting with the seeder, maybe 40 kg/mu compound — gives about 6 kg N as base. Then one topdress of urea at the big-trumpet stage (when the plants are knee-high, maybe end of July), about 20-25 kg urea per mu, another 10-11 kg N. So total N around 16-17 kg/mu for maize.

Irrigation: maize usually only needs 1-2 times — once after planting if it's dry to get it up, once at tasseling/silking which is the critical stage. Summer rains usually help.

Pesticide: spray herbicide after planting, and one insecticide spray for corn borer in mid-summer.

**Overall:**
My budget is tight but manageable. The off-farm income from my son helps cover inputs. I won't cut fertilizer because a bad yield hurts more than the money saved. I won't add more fertilizer either — what I do works, and I saw neighbors waste money on it. I'll stick with what I know.
